newsitem.title: USA: Daschle - would oppose US tax cuts $100 bln or more.
newsitem.headline: Daschle - would oppose US tax cuts $100 bln or more.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Thomas Daschle said Monday he would oppose tax cuts of $100 billion or more over five years and that the Clinton administration had put its "final offer" on Medicare savings on the table.

"I couldn't support a $100 billion in tax cuts today, and I would probably oppose a budget agreement that had that much in tax cuts," Daschle of South Dakota said. "We have a lot of members of our caucus who don't believe that under these circumstances that we ought to be cutting taxes at all," he told reporters.

Daschle said any tax cuts would have to stay in the "double-digits." President Clinton has proposed $98 billion in tax cuts over five years in his budget, while Senate Republicans want up to twice that amount.
The administration offering $18 billion more in Medicare savings during recent budget negotiations to bring total savings to $100 billion over five years was a "final offer," Daschle said.
"I think the $100 billion represents the outside parameter, probably the ceiling that is the limit beyond which we simply can't go," Daschle said.

"The administration has indicated to me personally, to the budget committee Democrats, that this is their final offer and I expect that it will be the final offer," he said, referring only to Medicare.
Formal budget negotiations between White House officials and congressional budget leaders were expected to resume Wednesday.
